question.:question/problem: Rewrite the expression $(x^{2} + 6x + 9) - 2$ as the difference between a perfect square and a constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we recall the following formula:

$$
{x}^{2}+2ax+{a}^{2}=(x+a{)}^{2}
$$

Notice that we have a perfect square in the parentheses that we can factor as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+6x+9 & =  \\ {x}^{2}+6x+{3}^{2} & =  \\ {x}^{2}+2\cdot 3x+{3}^{2} & =  \\ (x+3{)}^{2} & \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}+6x+9)-2 & = \\ (x+3{)}^{2}-2 & .\end{aligned}
$$
